extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners dealing with restriction practice (USPTO/MPEP audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how a restriction requirement may be made under 35 U.S.C. 121, tests for independence/distinctness of claimed inventions, showing serious search/examination burden, election of species, linking claims, and rejoinder/withdrawal procedures during patent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for restriction (35 U.S.C. 121)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more independent and distinct inventions are claimed in one application, the Director may require the application to be restricted to one of the inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction is the practice of requiring an applicant to elect a single, claimed invention for examination when two or more independent inventions and/or two or more distinct inventions are claimed. The terms 'independent' and 'distinct' are mutually exclusive alternative requirements; only one must be met to support restriction. (MPEP 802, 802.02)

rubrics_metrics.name: When restriction is proper (two basic criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper restriction requirement must: (i) show the inventions are independent or distinct as claimed, AND (ii) show that there would be a serious search and examination burden on the examiner if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction is at the examiner's discretion and is NOT a tool for reducing the number of claims for mere convenience. (MPEP 803(I))

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent inventions test
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are independent (unrelated) if there is no disclosed relationship between the inventions — i.e., they are unconnected in design, operation, and effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include items with different modes of operation/functions/effects (e.g., an article of apparel vs a locomotive), or a process and a product where the product cannot be used in or made by the process. Use FP 8.20.02 for unrelated inventions and FP 8.20.03 for unrelated product/process. (MPEP 802.01 I, 806.06)

rubrics_metrics.name: Related but distinct inventions test
rubrics_metrics.description: Related inventions are disclosed as connected in at least one of design, operation, or effect. They are distinct if, as claimed, they are not connected in at least one of design, operation, or effect and at least one invention is patentable (novel and nonobvious) over the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction can be required when related inventions are distinct and there would be a serious burden on the examiner. (MPEP 802.01 II and 806.05)

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing serious search and examination burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons must be provided why a serious search and examination burden would exist if restriction were not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious burden can be shown by one or more of: (a) separate classification (each invention a separate subject for inventive effort and separate field of search), (b) separate status in the art when classifiable together (e.g., patents showing separate inventive effort), (c) a different field of search (necessitating different search queries, groups/sub-groups, or electronic resources). (MPEP 803 II, 803.02, 806.05, 808.02; FP 8.21)

rubrics_metrics.name: When restriction is not appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction cannot be required when: no serious burden exists in searching/examining the claims; inventions are not distinct as claimed; there is an express admission that claimed inventions would have been obvious over each other (35 U.S.C. 103); or claims define the same essential characteristics of a single disclosed embodiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if claims are drawn to independent or distinct inventions, lack of serious burden prevents restriction. (MPEP 803, 806.03)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with non-statutory double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner indicates via restriction that inventions A and B are independent or patentably distinct, the examiner is generally prohibited from later asserting non-statutory double patenting between claims to A and B (with limited exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: a nonstatutory double patenting rejection may be proper if the restriction was withdrawn before the rejection, or if the examiner later determines the inventions are patentably indistinct and the later application is not a divisional maintaining consonance with the restriction. Improper restriction of patentably indistinct sets can result in multiple patents on indistinct variations. If unclear whether to restrict, ask whether you would apply a nonstatutory double patenting rejection if claims were in different applications: if yes, do not require restriction; if no, restriction may be appropriate but still requires showing serious burden. (MPEP 804.01, 804.01A-H)

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth vs patentable distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mistake variations in claim breadth for patentable distinctness. Claims should not be restricted if they define the same essential characteristics of a single disclosed embodiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims define the same essential characteristics when they provide different definitions of the same invention or vary only in breadth/scope (e.g., a broad claim and narrower dependent claims to the same structure). Such claims are not restrictable because they could serve as a basis for non-statutory double patenting if prosecuted separately. (MPEP 806.03)

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of related inventions to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Related-invention categories where distinctness analyses are applied include combination-subcombination; subcombinations usable together; process and apparatus for its practice; process of making and product made; apparatus and product made; product and process of using; product, process of making, and process of using; related products/processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories guide which distinctness tests apply (see MPEP 806.05(c)-(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination-subcombination two-way distinctness test
rubrics_metrics.description: To support a restriction between a combination and a subcombination, both (i) and (ii) must be met: (i) the combination as claimed does not require the particulars of the subcombination as claimed for patentability; AND (ii) the subcombination has utility either by itself or in another materially different combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these factors cannot both be shown, the inventions are not distinct. (MPEP 806.05(c); FP 8.15) Examples throughout the guidance illustrate ABsp–Bsp, ABbr–Bsp, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombinations usable together criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more claimed subcombinations disclosed as usable together are usually restrictable when: at least one subcombination can be shown to be separately usable or have utility other than in the disclosed combination; the subcombinations do not overlap in scope; and they are not obvious variants of one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Not overlapping in scope' means mutually exclusive limitations or limitations that would not read on each other. Serious burden must also be shown. When plural subcombinations usable together are present and a combination requires particulars of at least one subcombination, a two-way distinctness and serious burden must be shown. (MPEP 806.05(d); FP 8.16)

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and apparatus for its practice one-way test
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction between a process and an apparatus for its practice is based on a one-way test: (i) the process can be practiced by another materially different apparatus or by hand; OR (ii) the apparatus can be used to practice another materially different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one of these is true, restriction may be proper. (MPEP 806.05(e); FP 8.17)

rubrics_metrics.name: Process of making and product made one-way test
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction between a process of making and a product made is based on a one-way test: (i) the process is not an obvious process of making the product and can be used to make another materially different product; OR (ii) the product can be made by another materially different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this test to determine distinctness between process-of-making claims and product claims. (MPEP 806.05(f); FP 8.18)

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus and product made one-way test
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction between an apparatus and a product made by the apparatus is based on a one-way test: (i) the apparatus is not an obvious apparatus for making the product and can be used to make another materially different product; OR (ii) the product can be made by another materially different apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this test when apparatus claims and product claims coexist. (MPEP 806.05(g); FP 8.19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and process of using a product one-way test
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction between a product and a process of using the product is based on a one-way test: (i) the process of using as claimed can be practiced with another materially different product; OR (ii) the product can be used in a materially different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when product claims and method-of-use claims are both present. (MPEP 806.05(h); FP 8.20)

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-way distinctness for product / making / using
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims to product, process of making, and process of using are present, a three-way requirement for restriction can only be made when: (i) the process of making is distinct from the product, AND (ii) the process of using is distinct from the product, AND (iii) the process of making is distinct from the process of using.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If distinctness cannot be shown between process of making and the product, the process of using may be joined with process of making and the product. (MPEP 806.05(i))

rubrics_metrics.name: Related products or related processes two-way distinctness test
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction between related products or related processes is based on a two-way test: (i) the inventions as claimed do not overlap in scope, AND (ii) the inventions are not obvious variants, AND (iii) the inventions are not capable of use together or can have a materially different design, mode of operation, function, or effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All (or more than two, if applicable) claim groups in question must meet these criteria. (MPEP 806.05(j))

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species — when to require
rubrics_metrics.description: An election of species may be required when there are multiple patentably distinct embodiments (species) claimed and where there is a serious burden to the examiner to examine all of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct species are identified by figures or distinguishing characteristics; claims can be used for grouping when figures/descriptions are not convenient. Generic claims may or may not be present. (MPEP 808.01(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species two-prong test
rubrics_metrics.description: Each species, as claimed, must (i) require a mutually exclusive limitation, AND (ii) the species must not be obvious variants of each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election of species cannot be required when species are obvious variants, when examining together would not present a serious burden, or when claims are only directed to a single species with no generic claim. (MPEP 806.04(f); MPEP 803, 806.04, 809.02(a), 808.01(a), FP 8.01)

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush group guidance for election of species
rubrics_metrics.description: A Markush group (closed list of alternatives) may require election of species only between patentably distinct alternatives; patentably indistinct alternatives should be grouped together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific 'selected from the group consisting of …' wording is not required for Markush treatment. When an elected species in a proper Markush claim is found allowable, another species must be examined until one species is found in the prior art or until the entire Markush group is allowable. (MPEP 803.02 III(A); 2117)

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking claim rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A linking claim is a claim which, if allowable, links together claimed inventions that would otherwise be properly divisible (restrictable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a linking claim is found allowable, any restriction between linked claims must be withdrawn and the claims rejoined. The record should show withdrawal and identify which claims are rejoined. Linking claims are most commonly genus claims linking species or subcombination claims linking plural combinations. Restriction can still be required between distinct but linked inventions; if a linked invention is elected, linking claims are examined with the elected invention. (MPEP 809, 809.03)

rubrics_metrics.name: Election by original presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Election by original presentation limits subsequent prosecution to the initially-examined (acted upon) invention in a single application; applicants generally may not switch inventions after an election and an office action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCEs may not be used as a matter of right to shift inventions. Claims later presented to an independent/distinct invention may be withdrawn as non-elected. An amendment cancelling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims to the non-elected invention is non-responsive and should be notified via FP 8.26. Originally presented claims may be constructively elected even if no restriction was previously issued. The next office action should explain why new inventions are independent or distinct and include the election by original presentation form paragraph. (MPEP 706.06(h)VI(B), 818.02(a), 819, 821.03; MPEP 821.03)

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on election by original presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Election by original presentation is NOT applicable when: a provisional election of a single species in a Markush claim was made and the applicant later cancels the elected species; OR the applicant presents claims that could not have been restricted from the claims drawn to the elected invention had they been presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP for specific procedural references. (MPEP 803.02, 809.02(a), 808.01(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder eligibility and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejoinder is withdrawal of a restriction between an allowable elected invention and a non-elected invention and examination of the formerly non-elected invention on the merits; to be eligible, a claim to a non-elected invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejoined claims must be fully examined for patentability under 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, and 112 and any rejoinder must be clearly explained on the record. (MPEP 821.04)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner practices for rejoinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should consider rejoinder after each amendment and each time an office action is sent; if all elected claims with traverse are ready for allowance and rejoinder is NOT appropriate, the examiner must request permission to cancel non-elected claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an election was made without traverse, eligible non-elected species/inventions should be rejoined; non-elected claims may only be cancelled by examiner amendment when expressly authorized by applicant. (MPEP 821.01, 821.02, 821.04)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder of allowable linking claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When a linking claim is allowable, any restriction between the inventions it links cannot be maintained; rejoin pending claims that depend from or require all limitations of the allowable linking claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record must state the restriction withdrawal. Rejoined claims must be re-examined and the applicant may reintroduce canceled subject matter by amendment. Applicant need not request rejoinder. (MPEP 809, FP 8.01, FP 8.02, FP 8.12)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder relating to combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: If all claims directed to an elected combination invention are allowable, the examiner must reconsider any restriction between the combination and subcombinations and withdraw restriction where a subcombination is allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejoin any subcombinations that were searched and found allowable, and rejoin any non-elected claims that require all limitations of the allowable claim. (MPEP 806.05(d))

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder of process when product claim is allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: If elected product claim(s) are subsequently found allowable, consider withdrawing process claims which depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable product claim so they may be rejoined and examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims directed to a non-elected process invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable product claim to be rejoined. If applicant cancelled all claims to a non-elected process before rejoinder occurs, the examiner should not withdraw the restriction requirement to preserve rights under 35 U.S.C. 121. (MPEP 821.04(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary principle for restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is the requirement to elect one of two or more patentably distinct inventions for examination and is only proper when there would be a serious search and examination burden and the inventions are independent or distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction can prohibit a nonstatutory double patenting rejection when later divisional applications are filed (if maintained). Examiners must provide a proper basis for restriction and a clear record of withdrawal when appropriate. (Summary slide)
